summary.title: Microarchitectural comparison and in-core modeling of state-of-the-art CPUs: Grace, Sapphire Rapids, and Genoa
summary.one_liner: A 2024 arXiv paper comparing Nvidia Grace (Neoverse V2), Intel Sapphire Rapids (Golden Cove) and AMD Genoa (Zen 4) CPUs, with an in-core performance model built into OSACA and a study of write-allocate evasion.
keywords: single core vs full node performance
takeaways: Zen 4, Golden Cove and Neoverse V2 in-core behavior was modeled by extending OSACA and compared against LLVM-MCA.
Microbenchmarks and full-node measurements complement the single-core analysis of the three CPUs.
Grace Superchip is reported to have a next-to-optimal implementation of write-allocate evasion.
On Zen 4, avoiding write allocates is only possible by explicitly using non-temporal stores, according to the paper.
summary.summary: The paper analyzes three HPC-oriented CPUs: Nvidia Grace (Neoverse V2), Intel Sapphire Rapids (Golden Cove) and AMD Genoa (Zen 4). It starts with single-core peculiarities and extends the comparison with microbenchmarks and full-node capabilities. The authors build an in-core performance model for these microarchitectures by extending the OSACA tool and compare it with LLVM-MCA. A special focus is the write-allocate evasion feature, where the paper finds Grace near-optimal and Zen 4 requiring explicit non-temporal stores. The listing also describes fixed-clock in-core measurements and per-socket clocks under vector load, but the fetched page text is only the abstract and arXiv navigation.
